title: Two-step filtered module homotopy and derived categories
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A two-step filtered module complex is a monomorphism $i:K^\prime\to K$ of integer cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], representing the filtration $0\subset K^\prime\subset K$ [def-sp-filtration]. Morphisms are commutative squares of chain maps. Its two graded complexes are $K^\prime$ and $\operatorname{coker}(i)=K/K^\prime$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. A filtered homotopy from $f$ to $g$ is a chain homotopy on the total complexes satisfying $f-g=dh+hd$ whose components factor through the subcomplex inclusions. Let $KF_2(R)$ be the quotient by these homotopies, with canonical quotient functor $q$. Let $W_2$ be the homotopy classes having a chain-map representative that induces quasi-isomorphisms on both graded complexes. Define $DF_2(R)=KF_2(R)[W_2^{-1}]$, with functors $Q_h:KF_2(R)\to DF_2(R)$ and $Q=qQ_h$ from pairs of complexes. There is no cochain-degree bound. Restriction to the subcomplex and passage to the cokernel, followed by ordinary derived localization, send filtered homotopic maps to equal maps in $D(R)$; the resulting functors on $KF_2(R)$ invert $W_2$. The canonical graded functors $\operatorname{gr}^1,\operatorname{gr}^0:DF_2(R)\to D(R)$ are their localization lifts. Here $\operatorname{gr}^1$ is the subcomplex functor and $\operatorname{gr}^0$ the quotient functor, with their canonical chain-map normalization.
